key_insight: Weak sinusoidal forcing can strongly reshape turbulence and inertial-particle clustering in a planar jet even though the mean flow changes very little.
engineering_relevance: Small, low-frequency modulation offers a potential control knob for particle mixing, deposition, and separation in jet-driven systems without major changes to the average transport field.
method: Turbulent planar jet tested at two Reynolds numbers (~4950 and ~9900 based on nozzle height).
Applied sinusoidal forcing at a frequency three orders of magnitude below the jet’s preferred instability.
Measured carrier turbulence with hot-wire anemometry and particle clustering with high-speed imaging plus Voronoi tessellations.
evidence_signal: Across the forcing cycle, integral scale dropped by up to 40%, and preferential concentration varied by 21–49% of the cycle mean, with clustering peaking when the Kolmogorov time scale was largest.
watch_item: The forcing effects are strongly phase-dependent, so cycle-averaged metrics can hide large instantaneous changes in clustering and dissipation.
paper_title: Preferential concentration in a periodically forced particle-laden turbulent planar jet
